title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts match the record, and its documented controls and licensing are supported. It correctly distinguishes the planned model-driven app skill from other Cowork app-building experiences; minor clarifications concern a wizard heading and Microsoft's differing statements about low spending limits.

claims.claim: The spending-policy wizard is reached through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... Policy scope ... choose Identity as the scope. ... switch to Specific groups ... Select agents and services ... Set limits and alerts
claims.fix: Include the Policy scope heading: 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Policy scope > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts'. The Cowork service selection is also confirmed by the cited cowork-admin-governance page.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy with the specified Cowork service and credit limits.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: The beta create request uses serviceSettings with serviceId cowork and state enabled, plus periodLimit and perUserLimit.
claims.quote: "periodLimit": { ... "unit": "copilotCredit" }, "perUserLimit": { ... "unit": "copilotCredit" }, ... "serviceSettings": [ { "serviceId": "cowork", "state": "enabled" } ]

claims.claim: Group-scoped spending policies are created disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: A group policy's audience is linked before the service enables the policy.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.

claims.claim: Cowork access is granted by a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not block Cowork access for an in-scope user.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is. A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access.
claims.fix: Keep the access statement, but add: 'The spending-policy authoring page now requires at least 2,000 credits per user per month for new policies, although the Cowork access page still describes a one-credit policy as granting access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits#set-limits-and-alerts.

claims.claim: A user can start tasks after reaching a credit limit because enforcement is asynchronous.
